correctness.rationale: For the graph with edges lx,xy,xp,xq,yp,yq the function (l,x,y,p,q)=(0,2,1,0,0) has weight 3, and transfers x->l or y->p,q each leave an Italian dominating function. Exhaustive case splitting for weights <=2 proves the lower bound; a weight-three classification by (2,1) and (1,1,1) label types proves unique optimum. Transferring x->l produces (1,1,1,0,0), which is Italian but not secure Italian, disproving precisely the erroneous assertion of the published proof. Independent exact enumeration of every simple labeled graph on n=1..4 with degree-one vertices finds an optimal secure Italian labeling with all leaves 1, so order five is minimal among all graphs with leaves.
residual_risks: The five-vertex witness refutes only Lemma 1, not automatically the later theorems that cite it.
Exhaustive smaller-order classification is complete for simple labeled graphs with leaves, not for other domination rules.
